# Specification: Work-item mirror

## 1. Business Goal

<!-- last written by: spec-author, 2026-10-24 -->

The state of this repository's work - what is planned, what is blocked, what is done and which pull request delivered it - lives in `**/.issue/` work items and `epics/*/epic.md`, readable only from a clone with the queue script; on GitHub a reader finds one hand-filed issue and nothing of the roadmap, and a merged pull request names its item only in a commit body. This Feature removes that failure state without moving the record of truth: every push to `main` that changes an item or an epic brings a one-way, read-only set of GitHub issues into line with the tree - one marked issue per item and per epic, open or closed as the item is, linked to its parent and to the pull request that delivered it - and nothing on GitHub is ever read back into an item (decision 0001; migrating instead is rejected by decision 0002).

## 2. User Needs

<!-- last written by: spec-author, 2026-10-24 -->

| #   | Persona                                       | Need                                                                            | Pain Point Today                                      |
| --- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | A reader of the repository on GitHub          | The planned, open and done work, by epic and Feature, without a clone           | One hand-filed issue; the work is invisible on GitHub |
| 2   | A reader of a merged pull request             | The item the pull request delivered, linked from the pull request               | The item id is in the commit body only                |
| 3   | The maintainer                                | The mirror kept current by `main` with no hand step, and never a second tracker | Any GitHub presence would be kept by hand and drift   |
| 4   | `0101-F8`                                     | The work-item files kept as the tracker, so its rules have a tree to run on     | N/A (internal dependency)                             |
| 5   | The queue script and every specification link | The item files, their paths and their schema unchanged                          | N/A (internal dependency)                             |

### Assumptions

| ID  | Assumption                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A-1 | The scale on `main` at `6bccca3a` (2026-10-24) is 263 work items (181 `done`) and 12 epics, so the first run creates about 275 issues; repository `RLittlesII/specht` is public with issues enabled and one existing issue, #256, filed by hand.                                                                            |
| A-2 | Every change reaches `main` through a squash or rebase merge whose commit subject ends in `(#<pull request>)` (`0055-F8` B-001, B-004, B-005); 3 done items (`0003`, `0057`, `0097`) predate pull requests, and 22 done ids are named by more than one commit subject (review round 1), `0045` by #264 and #270 among them. |
| A-3 | The workflow's own token, with `issues: write`, can create labels, issues, comments and sub-issue links on this repository; it needs no repository setting toggled (`0055-F8`).                                                                                                                                             |
| A-4 | A run sees the full history of `main`, so the commit that delivered a done item can be found from git alone.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| A-5 | Id `0220` is claimed twice, by `.issue/0220-rule-page-versioning-spike.yml` and `.performance/benchmarks/Startup/.issue/0220-cold-start-baseline-bundled-framework.yml`; it is the only duplicate at 2026-10-24.                                                                                                            |

## 4. Constraints

<!-- last written by: spec-author, 2026-10-25 (item 0295) -->

| ID   | Constraint                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Rules Out                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| C-1  | The mirror writes nothing into the repository tree (decision 0001).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | A commit, push, branch or pull request from the mirror; an issue number written back into an item or a specification; a generated index of issues checked in.                                                                                          |
| C-2  | The mirror reads nothing from GitHub into an item (decision 0001).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | An item field, status or comment derived from an issue's state, labels, comments or edits; an issue edited by hand becoming the source of a later write to the tree.                                                                                   |
| C-3  | `github_mode` stays `false`, and the work item owns delivery state (AGENTS.md § SDLC; decision 0002).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | An issue as the record of an item's status; an item closed by closing its issue; `Closes #<issue>` in a commit as the way an item is delivered; a status label as an input to the queue script.                                                        |
| C-4  | Every path the mirror writes into an issue, a comment or the step summary is relative to the repository root (brief § 9).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | An absolute path; a runner workspace path; a path that names the machine the run happened on.                                                                                                                                                          |
| C-5  | The mirror authenticates with the workflow's own `GITHUB_TOKEN`, granted `issues: write`, `pull-requests: write` and `contents: read`, and nothing else.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | A personal access token or any repository secret; `contents: write`; any other permission the workflow's `permissions:` would otherwise grant; a GitHub App installation.                                                                              |
| C-6  | The mirror workflow is generated by the NUKE build and committed, as the `ci`, `main` and `renovate` workflows are (`0055-F2` C-1).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | A hand-written or hand-edited file under `.github/workflows/` for the mirror; a mirror workflow the build would not generate.                                                                                                                          |
| C-7  | The mirror is a Python script using only the standard library and the `gh` command, living under `.github/mirror/`; it reads items through the item reader in `.agents/skills/specht-conventions/scripts/next.py`, extended to key items by path and to read every field the mirror needs, and shared by the queue script and the mirror; the mirror may read an item file's raw text only for B-021 (decision 0007). | A third-party Python package; a second item parser, or a mirror-only copy of the reader, that can disagree with the queue script; mirror code in a .NET project; an extension that changes the queue script's output for a tree with no duplicated id. |
| C-8  | The item schema `.spec/templates/item.yml` is unchanged by this Feature.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | A mirror-only key in an item, such as an issue number or a sync stamp; a status value added for the mirror.                                                                                                                                            |
| C-9  | The packages `specht.tool` and `Specht.CodeAnalysis` are unaffected by this Feature.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | A change under `src/` for the mirror; a mirror dependency in `Directory.Packages.props`; a network call in the check (AGENTS.md § Invariants).                                                                                                         |
| C-10 | The mirror makes its writes to GitHub one at a time.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Concurrent or parallel writes to GitHub.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| C-11 | The mirror's plan computation is tested with the standard library's `unittest` against a fake `gh` and a synthetic git log, and the `MirrorTest` build target runs those tests (decision 0005; OQ-8).                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | A test that calls GitHub, reads this repository's own history or tree as its fixture, or needs a third-party test package; a plan computation no test runs.                                                                                            |
| C-12 | `github_issue` and `synced_at` stay `null` in every Feature specification and every epic, and the shipped Feature template is not edited for the mirror (ADR-0022).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | An issue number written into frontmatter by hand or by the mirror; a `synced_at` stamp; an edit to `.specht/templates/feature.md` or its embedded copy for the mirror.                                                                                 |
| C-13 | The scenarios in `work-item-mirror.feature` are proved by the tests § 9 names for each claim - the script's `unittest` tests, and the build tests that read the generated workflow file - and no Reqnroll step definition binds them (C-6, C-7, C-11).                                                                                                                                                                | A Reqnroll binding or step definition class for the mirror's scenarios; a .NET test that runs the mirror script; a claim counted as proved by a test § 9 does not name.                                                                                |

Not planned.                                                                                                                                                        |
| 10  | Running `MirrorTest` from the `Default` target or CI's pull-request build              | `0055-F1` owns the build targets and `0055-F2` the CI workflows, so wiring it in amends both first (OQ-8). A follow-up, not made here.                                                                                                              |
| 11  | Recovering a waiting run that a later run replaced                                     | GitHub keeps one pending run per concurrency group (B-040). The next run brings every issue into line (B-031), but the replaced push's `Delivers` comments (B-024) are posted only by a manual backfill run (B-027). No new mechanism; not planned. |

## 6. Concern Separation

<!-- last written by: implementer, 2026-10-25 (item 0295) -->

| #   | Concern                                                                               | Classification |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| 1   | Which files are mirrored, and how a file finds its issue (the marker)                 | Business       |
| 2   | Title, labels and open or closed state, derived from frontmatter                      | Business       |
| 3   | What a body shows: provenance, Delivered by, rendered fields, the file, the footer    | Business       |
| 4   | Which commit and pull request delivered a done item, derived from the history of main | Both           |
| 5   | One `Delivers` comment per item and pull request, and the backfill                    | Business       |
| 6   | Writing only what differs, so a rerun converges and a matching tree writes nothing    | Technical      |
| 7   | Reaching GitHub through `gh`, one write at a time, and a dry run that writes nothing  | Technical      |
| 8   | One item reader shared with the queue script                                          | Technical      |
| 9   | A marked issue whose file is gone: kept, labelled `stale`, warned about               | Business       |
| 10  | The step summary: counts, skipped reasons, stale warnings                             | Both           |
| 11  | When a run starts: the push and dispatch triggers, the path filter, one queue         | Business       |
| 12  | The run's token and its three permissions, and a checkout of the full history         | Technical      |

## 7. Technical Design

<!-- last written by: implementer, 2026-10-25 (item 0295) -->

Delivered by items `0294` and `0295`. The script is [`../mirror_items.py`](../mirror_items.py); the reader is `read_items` in [`next.py`](../../../.agents/skills/specht-conventions/scripts/next.py); the workflow is generated from [`SpechtBuild.Mirror.cs`](../../../.build/SpechtBuild.Mirror.cs) into [`mirror.yml`](../../workflows/mirror.yml).

- **The shared reader (C-7).** `read_items(root)` keys each item by its repository-relative path, so both `0220` files survive (B-023). The id still comes from the file name's first four digits. It now also reads `type` and, through `listing`, `acceptance_criteria`, `decisions` and `out_of_scope`: block entries (`- |`), quoted entries (a double-quoted one decoded as JSON, falling back to its text), plain entries and a flow list (`["…"]`), each with its whitespace collapsed. Entries split only at the first entry's indentation, so a `- ` inside a `|` block stays in its entry. The queue's `main` re-indexes the items by id, the last file walked winning as before. Its output is therefore unchanged on every tree, this one included: `.performance/…/0220-cold-start-…` (done) still hides `.issue/0220-rule-page-versioning-spike.yml` (ready) from the queue, as it did before the change. That is a queue defect this Feature does not fix.
- **One run** is `mirror(root, gh, history, *, pushed, backfill)`, in this order. Every step compares the plan with what `gh` reports now, so an interrupted run is finished by the next (B-031), and a tree that matches writes nothing (B-029).
  1. `parse_history` splits the `git log` text (§ 8) on `\x1e`. It records, per commit, the `**/.issue/*.yml` paths whose `+++ b/` section adds a `status: done` line. `--no-renames` makes a moved item an added file, so its new path counts.
  2. `read_tree` reads the epics (`epics/*/epic.md`, sorted) and then the items (sorted by path). An epic's frontmatter is read with the queue's `scalar`. Ids are counted across both, and the marker is the id, or `<id> <path>` when more than one file claims it (B-003, B-049, decision 0004). Each body is rendered.
  3. The issues are read once. Each `<!-- specht-item: … -->` marker indexes its issue, and the lowest number wins a repeat. An issue with no marker is never indexed, so nothing touches it (B-032). A marked issue whose marker no file has is an orphan.
  4. Every label the plan applies that `labels()` lacks is created first, in one pass before any issue write (B-011).
  5. Per file: a missing issue is created with its title, body and labels (B-001, B-002). An existing one gets one `edit_issue` holding only what differs (B-030). The fields compared are the title, the body (compared with `\r\n` folded and the ends trimmed) and the owned labels. The owned labels are `mirrored`, `goal`, `stale`, `type:*` and `status:*`; any other label, such as `wontfix`, is left as it is. Then comes the state. `done` closes as `completed`, re-closing an issue closed `not_planned`; anything else reopens (B-012, B-013, B-045, B-046).
  6. A `parent` that exactly one file claims, item or epic, is linked with `add_sub_issue` when the child's current parent differs (B-014, B-015). The children per parent are counted from the issues as read. At 100 the link is not attempted, and is skipped and named instead (OQ-4 default).
  7. Each orphan without `stale` gets `stale` added, and nothing else. It is never closed, and the `gh` surface has no delete (B-033, B-034). Every orphan is warned about, labelled this run or not (B-035).
  8. Delivery comments: a pushed commit's done path for an item that is done now comments `Delivers #<issue> (<id>).` on the pull request its subject names (B-024). A pushed commit that names none counts as skipped (B-025). `backfill` adds every done item whose Delivered by is a pull request (B-027). A body already among that pull request's comments, read once per pull request per run, is not posted again (B-026). Pull-request bodies have no write in the surface (B-028).
- **Labels** (B-004, B-007 to B-010, B-043, B-044, B-050): `mirrored`; `type:<type>` (`type:epic` for an epic); `status:<status>` unless `done`; `goal` for an item whose id `.issue/.goal` lists, read with the queue's `read_goal`.
- **Titles**: `<id>: <title>`, and `Epic <id>: <name>`, where the name is the frontmatter `title` with a leading `Epic <id>: ` removed (B-005, B-006).
- **Body**, in this order:
  - the marker;
  - `Mirrored from `<path>`on`main`.` (B-016);
  - for a done item, `Delivered by #<n>.` or `Delivered by <sha>.`;
  - one `Id <id> is also claimed by `<path>`.` line per other claimant (B-023);
  - the rendered sections. An item has `## Summary`, `## Acceptance criteria`, `## Decisions` and `## Out of scope`, each only when non-empty and the lists as bullets (B-020). An epic has `## Summary` from its `## Summary` section, or else its `description` (B-047, B-051);
  - `## Source`, holding the file verbatim, trailing newlines trimmed, in a `yaml` or `markdown` fence. The fence is one backtick longer than the longest backtick run that starts a line in the file, and at least three, so an epic's own fences cannot close it (B-021, B-048). A body over GitHub's limit links the file instead (B-052, below);
  - a rule, and the read-only footer (B-022).
- **Delivered by** (`delivered_by`, decision 0009) takes the first commit whose `done` paths include the file. If its subject ends `(#<n>)`, the answer is `#<n>` (B-017). Otherwise it is the last commit whose subject matches `<type>(<id>)[!]: … (#<n>)` (B-018). Otherwise it is that first commit's full sha (B-019). A done item with no such commit gets no line. The dry run lists it under "Done with no Delivered by line".
- **`gh`.** `Gh` is the real adapter. It reads issues through one paginated GraphQL query (number, title, body, state, state reason, labels, parent, node id). It reads labels with `gh label list` and a pull request's comments with the paginated REST comments endpoint. It writes with `gh label create`, `gh issue create` and `gh issue edit` (bodies on standard input), `gh api -X PATCH` for close (with `state_reason`) and reopen, GraphQL `addSubIssue` with `replaceParent: true`, and `gh pr comment`. Each call is a blocking `subprocess.run`, so writes are made one at a time (C-10). A failed call raises an error naming the subcommand and `gh`'s message, and the run stops; the next run converges. `Plan` wraps `Gh` for `--dry-run`. It passes the reads through and records the writes, giving a created issue the placeholder number `new-<n>`.
- **CLI.** `python3 .github/mirror/mirror_items.py (--dry-run | --apply) [--repo <owner/name>] [--backfill] [--before <sha> --after <sha>] [--json] [--root <dir>]`. `--repo` defaults to `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, then to `gh repo view`. `history` is `git log --reverse --first-parent --format=%x1e%H%x1f%s -p --unified=0 --no-renames --no-color HEAD`. `pushed` is `git rev-list --first-parent <before>..<after>`; it is `<after>` alone when `--before` is absent or all zeros, and nothing without `--after`. The step summary is appended to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` when that is set, a runner file outside the tree. `--apply` prints the step summary. `--dry-run` prints the step summary, the done items with no Delivered by line and a table of planned writes, or with `--json` the counts, reasons and every write with its full body. Under C-1 the dry run prints to standard output only and writes no file into the tree, `.artifacts/` included.
- **Paths (C-4).** Every path in a body, a comment or the summary is the reader's repository-relative key, or an epic path made relative to the root. The root itself is never written.
- **`step_summary`** prints `## Work-item mirror`, one `- <kind>: <n>` line per count, then `### Skipped` with one reason per skip, then `### Stale` with one `Warning: #<n> …` line per orphan (B-035, B-041).
- **The build target (C-11, OQ-8).** `./build.sh MirrorTest` in [`.build/SpechtBuild.cs`](../../../.build/SpechtBuild.cs) runs `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s .github/mirror/tests -v` from the root. It fails on a non-zero exit. `-B` writes no `__pycache__` into the tree (`0055-F1` C-5). Its output is logged at information, because `unittest` reports on standard error. It has no dependency and is in neither `Default` nor CI's pull-request build: wiring it in amends `0055-F1` and `0055-F2`, which is spec-author's to write first (OQ-8). The amendment is a `.DependsOn(MirrorTest)` on `Test`, followed by regenerating `ci.yml` and `main.yml`.
- **GitHub's body limit (decision 0010; B-021, B-048, B-052, B-053).** `fitted` renders the body in full, and keeps it when it is at most `BODY_LIMIT`, 65,536 characters. Otherwise it renders `## Source` as one Markdown link to `https://github.com/<repo>/blob/<sha>/<path>`, where `<sha>` is the newest commit in `history`, the commit the run mirrors (`main` when the history is empty), and `<repo>` is the `repo` the `gh` it is handed names (`Gh` and `Plan` carry it). If that is still over, it also leaves out every rendered section after `## Summary`. The marker, provenance, Delivered by, claimant lines and footer are in every form. A body still over after both steps is written as it is, and GitHub refuses it (OQ-10's default). On this repository's tree on 2026-10-25, epic `0201`'s body, 101,914 characters in full, is 28,566 with its file linked; no body needs the second step, and the largest, epic `0132`'s, is 51,210 and keeps its file.
- **The workflow (item `0295`; B-036 to B-040, C-5, C-6, A-4).** `SpechtBuild.Mirror.cs` follows `SpechtBuild.Renovate.cs`: a `GitHubActionsSteps` attribute named `mirror` on `ubuntu-latest` (OQ-5's default), and `MirrorMiddleware` as its enhancement. The generator expresses every part. The attribute's `OnPushBranches` and `OnPushIncludePaths` give the push to `main` on the four paths (B-036, B-038, B-039). The middleware adds:
  - a `workflow_dispatch` trigger with a `boolean` input `backfill`, default `false` (B-037);
  - a workflow-level concurrency group `mirror` with `cancel-in-progress: false` (B-040);
  - permissions `None` with `contents: read`, `issues: write` and `pull-requests: write` (C-5);
  - two steps: a checkout with `fetch-depth: 0` (A-4), then one bash step. That step runs `python3 .github/mirror/mirror_items.py --apply --repo "${{ github.repository }}" --before "${{ github.event.before }}" --after "${{ github.event.after }}"`, adds `--backfill` through `${{ inputs.backfill && '--backfill' || '' }}`, and sets `GH_TOKEN` to `${{ github.token }}`.

  `--after` is `github.event.after`, not `github.sha`. A manual start has no push event, so both arguments are empty, `pushed` is empty and only `backfill` posts comments. With `github.sha`, a manual start would count the head commit as pushed. `./build.sh Compile` writes the file. The regeneration added `mirror.yml` and changed no other workflow, `ci.yml` and `main.yml` included (C-6).

- **Not reached by a test**: the `Gh` adapter, the CLI and the cap in step 6, which item `0296`'s first run exercises (§ 8). The dry run against this repository on 2026-10-25 used the `Gh` reads only. No run of the workflow has been observed; the first is item `0296`'s.

## 8. Testing Strategy

<!-- last written by: test-writer, 2026-10-25 -->

- **Where and how they run (C-11, decision 0005).** Standard-library `unittest` in [`../tests/`](../tests/): `test_mirror_items.py` for the script, `test_item_reader.py` for the shared reader C-7 extends, and `support.py` holding the fake `gh`, the synthetic git log writer and the temporary-tree writer both files use. Every test writes a synthetic tree into its own temporary directory with repository-relative paths; none reads this repository's tree or history, calls GitHub, runs `git` or reads a clock. OQ-8's target runs, from the repository root, `python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/mirror/tests -v`; it exits non-zero on any failure. No fixture directory is named `.issue`, so neither the queue script nor the mirror's own run picks a test tree up.
- **Two tiers, one runner.** The mechanisms (`parse_history`, `delivered_by`, the reader) are tested directly. Every other claim is tested end to end through `mirror()` over a temporary tree and the fake `gh`, which is the plan computation decision 0005 names, observed through the writes it makes. The `.feature` scenarios are not bound to Reqnroll: C-7 and C-11 put the mirror outside .NET and name `unittest` as its runner, so a step class would have to shell out to Python. Each test is named for its claim instead, and § 9 cites it. The gap this section reported, whether the scenarios need a binding of their own, is closed by C-13: the `unittest` tests § 9 names prove them, and no Reqnroll step definition binds them.
- **The seam the tests define**, which `implementer` builds to (`.github/mirror/mirror_items.py`):
  - `mirror(root, gh, history, *, pushed=(), backfill=False) -> Summary` reads the tree under `root` (items through `next.py`'s `read_items`, epics from `epics/*/epic.md`, goal ids from `.issue/.goal`), plans against `gh`, and applies the plan through `gh`, one write at a time. `history` is the text of `git log --reverse --first-parent --format=%x1e%H%x1f%s -p --unified=0 --no-renames` on `main`; `pushed` is the shas of the push's commits (B-024, B-025); `backfill` is B-027's input. `Summary.counts` has exactly the keys `created`, `edited`, `closed`, `reopened`, `linked`, `commented`, `stale` and `skipped`.
  - `parse_history(text) -> list` of commits oldest first, each with `.sha`, `.subject` and `.done`: the repository-relative paths of `**/.issue/*.yml` files whose diff in that commit adds `status: done`. A commit with no diff is kept; a diff of any other file is ignored.
  - `delivered_by(path, item_id, commits) -> str`: `"#<n>"` for a pull request (B-017, B-018), or the full sha (B-019).
  - `step_summary(summary) -> str`: the Markdown the run appends to the step summary, one line per count, naming each count with its number, and one warning line per stale issue naming `#<n>` (B-035, B-041).
  - The `gh` the script is handed (the fake implements it, the real one shells out to the `gh` command): `repo`, the `<owner>/<name>` its issues live in, which a link to a file at a commit names (B-052); reads `issues()` (every issue, with `number`, `title`, `body`, `state`, `state_reason`, `labels`, `parent`), `labels()` and `pr_comments(pr)`; writes `create_label(name)`, `create_issue(title, body, labels) -> number`, `edit_issue(number, title=None, body=None, add_labels=(), remove_labels=())`, `close_issue(number, reason)`, `reopen_issue(number)`, `add_sub_issue(parent, child)` and `comment_pr(pr, body)`. It has no pull-request edit and no delete; a call to either fails the test that makes it (B-028, B-033). The fake refuses a label the repository lacks (B-011) and can be set to stop after a number of writes (B-031).
  - `next.py`'s `read_items(root)` keys each item by its repository-relative path and adds `type`, `acceptance_criteria`, `decisions` and `out_of_scope` (lists of strings; `[]` when empty) to the fields it reads today (C-7).
- **Red for the right reason.** Today every `mirror_items` test fails on the assertion that the module exists, and the two reader tests fail on the id-keyed dictionary. Against a stub that imports and does nothing, all 53 script and reader tests fail on an assertion and none errors; B-029, B-033, B-042 and C-4 each assert first that the run wrote something, so an empty run cannot pass them. `test_C7_TreeWithNoDuplicatedId_WhenQueued_ShouldPrintTheQueueAsBeforeTheReaderChange` passes today by design: it pins the queue script's output for a tree with no duplicated id, captured from `next.py` before the change, and goes red only if the extension changes it. Against the script as built before decision 0010, the B-052 and B-053 tests fail on their link assertion (no line links the file), and the 57 tests run, 55 passing.
- **Mechanism and test, per claim** (B-036 to B-040 are item `0295`'s, under "The generated workflow" below):
  - B-001, B-002: the marker lookup that finds an existing issue instead of creating one, a decision; run twice, one issue. B-003, B-049: the marker, plain for an id one file claims and naming the path when more than one does (decision 0004), a derivation. B-023: the same id count, plus the other path in the body.
  - B-004, B-007, B-010, B-043: the label set derived from `type`, `.issue/.goal` and the epic kind, a derivation. B-008, B-009, B-044, B-050: the one `status:` label, or none when `done`, with stale ones removed, a derivation and a diff. B-011: the label diff against `labels()`, ordered before the write applying it, an ordering.
  - B-005, B-006: the title derivation. B-012, B-013, B-045, B-046: the state decision from `status`. B-014, B-015: `parent` resolved to an item's or an epic's issue, a mapping.
  - B-016, B-020, B-021, B-022, B-047, B-048, B-051: the body renderer, a mapping; the rendered parts are asserted above the fenced block so the verbatim copy cannot satisfy them, and B-048's epic contains a fence of its own.
  - B-021, B-048, B-052, B-053 (decision 0010): the body's length against GitHub's 65,536 characters, a boundary, then a fallback ordering. An epic padded so its body is exactly the limit keeps the file verbatim (B-048, passing today by design: it goes red if the boundary moves inside the limit); one character more replaces the copy with one Markdown link to `<repo>/blob/<sha>/<path>`, where `<sha>` is the newest commit in `history`, the commit the run mirrors (B-052). A work item whose acceptance criteria alone exceed the limit keeps its Summary and the link and renders none of its criteria, decisions or out-of-scope entries (B-053). The padding is measured from the body the run itself renders for the unpadded file, so the fixture needs no copy of the renderer. That the kept lines (marker, provenance, Delivered by, claimants, footer) survive is decision 0010's, not B-052's or B-053's, and each is pinned unconditionally by B-003, B-016, B-017, B-019, B-022 and B-023.
  - B-017, B-018, B-019: `parse_history` and `delivered_by` (decision 0009), unit-tested on their own, plus the "Delivered by" line in the body for B-017 and B-019.
  - B-024 to B-028: the delivery-comment decision over `pushed`, `backfill` and `pr_comments`. B-028 also rests on the `gh` surface having no pull-request edit.
  - B-029, B-030, B-031: the field diff between the planned and the current issue, observed as the writes made; B-031 compares an interrupted run, finished, with an uninterrupted one by marker.
  - B-032: issues without a marker are left out of the plan, a filter. B-033, B-034, B-035: a marked issue with no file is labelled `stale` and warned about, never closed, a decision.
  - B-041: the counts and `step_summary`. B-042, C-1: the tree's bytes before and after a run over an issue changed by hand. C-4: no write and no summary names the temporary root. C-10: the fake records that no write began while another was in progress.
  - C-7: `test_item_reader.py`, two claims of the reader and the unchanged queue output.
- **The generated workflow (item `0295`; B-036 to B-040, C-5, C-6, A-4).** These claims are literal settings in `.github/workflows/mirror.yml`, which the build generates (C-6), so the tests read that file rather than run it. `0055-F2` § 8 left the CI workflow's mechanisms untested and item `0073` carried that to `renovate.yml`; the later precedent is `CodeAnalysisReleaseIntegrationTests` in `test/build.tests`, which parses the generated `release.yml` with YamlDotNet and asserts its steps, and this section follows it. [`MirrorWorkflowIntegrationTests`](../../../test/build.tests/MirrorWorkflow.Integration.Tests.cs), tier Integration because it reads a committed file, parses the workflow once per test. None runs the mirror script, which C-13 rules out for a .NET test; what the script does with its arguments is the `unittest` tests' above.
  - B-036: `on.push` has `branches` exactly `main` and `paths` exactly the four patterns, in order, and the one step that runs the script passes `--apply`, the repository, and the push's `github.event.before` and `github.event.after` as `--before` and `--after`, the range B-024's `pushed` is read from.
  - B-037: `on.workflow_dispatch` declares a `boolean` input `backfill`, default `false`, and the step adds `--backfill` only through that input. B-027's backfill rests on this flag.
  - B-038: `on.push` carries only `branches` and `paths`, and no path is `**` or a negation, so a push touching none of the four starts nothing.
  - B-039: `on` has exactly `push` and `workflow_dispatch`, so no `pull_request` trigger exists, and the push names `main` alone.
  - B-040: the workflow-level `concurrency` has `group: mirror` and `cancel-in-progress: false`. GitHub queues the second run behind the first. It keeps at most one pending run per group: a third start while one runs and one waits replaces the waiting one. That is GitHub's rule, not the workflow's, and no test can observe it.
  - C-5: every permission but `contents: read`, `issues: write` and `pull-requests: write` is `none`, the step's `GH_TOKEN` is `${{ github.token }}`, and the file names no `secrets.`.
  - C-6: the file carries the generator's `<auto-generated>` header naming `GitHubActions_mirror`, and its `name` is `mirror`. That it matches what `./build.sh Compile` writes is the review of the regeneration diff, not a test.
  - A-4: the checkout step sets `fetch-depth: 0` and comes before the mirror step.
  - Red for the right reason: before item `0295`, every one of these tests fails on the assertion that `mirror.yml` exists.
- **§ 9 status.** A row naming a test is `Partial`: the test exists and fails until item `0294` builds the script and the reader change, and it becomes `Covered` when its tests pass. B-036 to B-040 were `Partial` until item `0295` generated the workflow, and are `Covered` since its tests pass.
- **Testability, reported to `implementer`.** The design is testable as the seam above states it. Two things the tests cannot reach: the real `gh` adapter, which shells out and is exercised only by item `0296`'s first run, and OQ-4's sub-issue cap, which has no claim and no test. The tests fix the git log invocation and the `gh` surface above; a different shape is a change to this section first.
- **The `@B-030` finding, answered.** This section reported that the `@B-030` scenario changed the item's title, which under B-021 also changes the body. The scenario now edits the issue's title by hand and keeps the body and labels matching (commit `9a6723c6`), which is what `test_B030_IssueTitleEditedByHand_WhenMirrored_ShouldWriteOnlyTheTitle` already arranges; test and scenario agree, and the test is unchanged.
